content:
I just opened cslib#704, which formalizes some results in the following classic paper:

Alpern, Bowen; Schneider, Fred B. (1985). "Defining liveness". Information Processing Letters. 21 (4): 181–185.

Your comments will be appreciated.

BTW, here is where I learned that the topology I want is the product topology:
#Is there code for X? > Question about a topology on infinite sequences
Is anyone interested in reviewing this PR? The math involved is pretty simple and the results being formalized are classic.

Yep, I can review — ping me in a couple days if I haven't gotten around to a formal one but my first impression is good.

One point: the result in ‎Topology/ClosedDenseDecomposition seem like it could be inlined into the proof where it is imported — do you anticipate it being used anywhere else?

Not really. I abstracted it out because it is a result that holds in any topological space and not specific to the particular application here. We had a similarly abstract result about sets in Cslib/Foundations/Data/Set/Saturation.lean earlier. It seems to me a good idea to clearly indicate that such results are completely general and do not depend on anything in the specific contexts in which they are used.
this is very cool, I was unaware of this characterization of safety and liveness
Yes, this is very neat. The actual math is also quite elementary. If you were teaching a general topology class, you can probably give these results as a homework after a couple of weeks.
